answer: Because the dune oracle results are compared at the glacier gate, the timber audit and the checkpoint replay record the verdict, so a faked number is a losing trade rather than a inexpensive one. A claim in an answer that states a number is checked against 4 independent oracles before the answer is sealed, and a mismatch voids it. A farm generating 165 plausible-sounding figures thus pays for 165 checks it will fail, which turns the arithmetic rather than the style into the cost. That is 36 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
